x_failures: Cites Dyscolus p.184 for beans having 'the same substance as human heads' or appearing 'like a human child' when buried, but the page says only that a peeled bean looks like genitals and that a boiled bean left under the moon produces blood. Also captions Rivinus p.267 as 'Faba minor (the broad bean)', but that page shows white lupine.
reason: Y's quotations from Hierocles p.181, Beroaldo p.212, Taylor p.12 and the Golden Ass p.71 all appear on those pages, though the Taylor and linen passages say little about beans. X covers useful ground, but it misstates what p.184 says and mislabels the lupine illustration as a bean.
